questions.question: What is Gross Combination Weight?

options.text: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo combined
The total weight of a single vehicle without cargo
The maximum weight the manufacturer allows

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the truck, trailer, and cargo combined
questions.explanation: Gross Combination Weight is the total weight of the truck, all trailers, and the cargo being carried.

questions.question: Is it good to keep space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: Yes, it gives you time to react to problems.
Only if you have a passenger with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it gives you time to react to problems.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your vehicle on all sides. This gives you time to react safely if something goes wrong.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?

options.text: Keep driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to get there sooner.
Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, stop and rest. Driving while tired is dangerous and causes crashes. Energy pills do not help because once they wear off, you will be even more tired.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment quickly?

options.text: When they are used a lot.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes can go out of adjustment quickly. Check your brakes often. Your vehicle needs all brakes working properly and adjusted correctly to stay safe.

questions.question: What is the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle during a leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should not lose more than 6 psi per minute during a leakage test. Know the safe limits for your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do with water and oil that builds up in your air brake system?

options.text: Leave it there—it helps the system work.
Let it take up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and oil that build up in your air brake system can damage it. Use the tank drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too fast.

questions.question: Can hydroplaning happen at low speeds?

options.text: No, only at very high speeds.
Yes, it can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
It happens most when tire pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is more likely if tire pressure is too low or tread is worn.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a red light

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before each trip starts. The trailer should be straight when you adjust your mirrors.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Use the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
Swerve side to side to get attention.
Turn all lights on and off several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Tap your brake pedal lightly several times to flash your brake lights. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: What do you test by pulling out the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before every trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to the emergency position. Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: When you start the engine of a truck with a trailer, how do you know the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, the dashboard lights should come on and then turn off. If the ABS warning light stays on, there is a problem. On a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear stays on after starting, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors when changing lanes?
questions.explanation: You should check your mirrors regularly while driving. When changing lanes, check them even more often than usual.

questions.question: How often should you check your cargo after it is secured?

options.text: You do not need to check it again for the entire trip.
You can wait at least eight hours before checking it.
You should check it every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check it every three hours or every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check your cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer than driving during the day?
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see hazards in the dark.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: how far you see ahead, how far you travel while reacting, brake lag distance, and actual braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leak rate for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: On a static leakage test for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes, the leak rate must not exceed 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. It needs repair.

questions.question: What color are the ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps. These lamps turn on when the ABS is not working. Find the malfunction lamp on your vehicle before you start driving.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If the signal goes off while driving, pull over and stop. Have the system checked and repaired.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before every trip starts. Make any needed adjustments at that time.
